stem: A living will and a health care proxy or durable power of attorney for health care are examples of what type of document?
rationale: Medicare describes an advance directive as a legal document that records future medical-treatment wishes if a person becomes unable to make decisions. It identifies a health care proxy or durable power of attorney as the person designated to make health decisions and a living will as the document describing desired treatments.
educational_objective: Recognize living wills and health care proxies or durable powers of attorney for health care as forms of advance directives.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / Medicare
source_locator: Description > Advance directives include 2 parts: health care proxy/durable power of attorney and living will
source_claim_supported: Advance directives document future health care wishes and may include a health care proxy or durable power of attorney and a living will.
correction_summary: Replaced the nonauthoritative POLST attribution with current Medicare/CMS guidance and simplified the choices while preserving the validated distinction between advance-directive document types.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by Medicare. B, C, and D are categorically different documents and do not describe living wills or health care proxies. No second answer remains.
